input:
I pasted a long document below, a bit of reading from earlier today.


### `[layer]` (required)

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | list | required, non-empty | Blocks applied in order inside every layer, e.g. `["attn", "ffn"]`. Each name selects the table `[layer.<name>]`. Blocks: `attn`, `gdn`, `ffn`, `moe`. |
| `pattern_by_layer` | string | none | Hybrid models: the `config.json` key holding a per-layer type list. Must equal `[config] layer_types` (default `"layer_types"`). When set, layer *i* uses `by_type[layer_types[i]]` instead of `pattern`. |
| `by_type` | table of lists | empty | Needs `pattern_by_layer`. One block list per layer type, e.g. `linear_attention = ["gdn", "moe"]`. A layer type with no entry is a load error. |
| `norms` | table of strings | empty | `pre_<block> = "<norm tensor prefix>"`: the norm applied before that block (`pre_attn`, `pre_ffn`, `pre_gdn`, `pre_moe`). |

### `[layer.attn]` (grouped-query attention)

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | required | `"gqa"`. Others (MLA, sliding window, Mamba) are not implemented. |
| `q`, `k`, `v`, `o` | string | required | Projection tensor prefixes. |
| `q_norm`, `k_norm` | string | none (no qk-norm) | Per-head RMSNorm on q / k before rope (Qwen3 has it; Llama and Qwen2 do not). |
| `rope` | string | `"default"` | Rotary variant. `"default"` is neox / rotate-half with `rope_theta` from `config.json` over the first `partial_rotary_factor * head_dim` values of each head. The scaling type (`rope_type`) is read from `config.json`, not the recipe; only the unscaled embedding is supported on `main`. |
| `gated` | bool | `false` | `q` projects to `[n_heads, 2 * head_dim]`: the query plus a per-head output gate (`attn_out * sigmoid(gate)` before `o`), interleaved per head (HF `attn_output_gate`, Qwen3.5/3.6). |

Projection biases (`q_bias`, `k_bias`, `v_bias`, Qwen2 style) and `llama3` / `yarn` rope scaling are added by draft PR
#77 (lane fx4); until it merges, a checkpoint with biases or scaled rope is refused at load with a message naming the
missing feature.

### `[layer.gdn]` (Gated DeltaNet linear attention: Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6)

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | required | `"gated_delta_net"`. |
| `in_qkv` | string | required | Fused q/k/v projection `[2*Hk*dk + Hv*dv, hidden]`. |
| `in_z` | string | required | Output-gate projection `[Hv*dv, hidden]`. |
| `in_b` | string | required | Beta projection `[Hv, hidden]`. |
| `in_a` | string | required | Decay projection `[Hv, hidden]`. |
| `conv` | string | required | Depthwise causal conv taps `[C, 1, K]` or `[C, K]`. |
| `a_log`, `dt_bias` | string | required | Decay parameters. |
| `norm` | string | required | Gated RMSNorm weight `[dv]` (plain weight, never offset by `norm_offset`). |
| `out` | string | required | Output projection. |

### `[layer.conv]` (gated short conv: Liquid LFM2 / LFM2.5)

The block is `y = out(C * causalconv(B * x))` with `[B | C | x] = in_proj(n)`; the depthwise conv has `K = conv_L_cache` taps, no
activation, no bias (`Op::ShortConv`, `crates/intarsia-core/src/model/short_conv.rs`). Its only state is the last `K - 1` columns of
`B * x`, a `Recurrent` slot like GatedDeltaNet's. The width is `hidden_size`. Pre-norm key: `layer.norms.pre_conv`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | required | `"short_conv"`. |
| `in_proj` | string | required | Projection `[3 * hidden, hidden]`; its rows split into `B`, `C`, `x`. |
| `conv` | string | required | Depthwise causal conv taps `[hidden, 1, K]` or `[hidden, K]`. |
| `out` | string | required | Output projection `[hidden, hidden]`. |

### `[layer.ffn]` (dense MLP)

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | required | `"dense"`. |
| `act` | string | required | `"silu_glu"` (SwiGLU). Other activations (GELU, ...) are not implemented; `recipe new` leaves a TODO. |
| `gate`, `up`, `down` | string | required | Projection tensor prefixes. |

### `[layer.moe]` (sparse mixture of experts, with shared expert)

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | required | `"qwen3_5_moe"` (the only MoE layout implemented: routed experts plus a gated shared expert). |
| `prefix` | string | required | Tensor prefix of the MoE block, e.g. `"model.language_model.layers.{i}.mlp"`; the loader finds router, experts and shared expert under it. Expert counts and widths come from `config.json`. |

### `[layer.gemma]` (Gemma 4 decoder layer, one block per layer)

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | required | `"gemma4"` (the only layout implemented). |
| `prefix` | string | required | Tensor prefix of the whole layer, e.g. `"model.language_model.layers.{i}"`. Everything under it (attention, dense MLP, router, experts, the five norms, `layer_scalar`) is found by the fixed Gemma 4 names. Head sizes, KV heads, sliding window, rope tables, soft-cap and expert counts come from `config.json` (`ModelDims::gemma`, `layer_types`). Use `pattern = ["gemma"]` and `[layer.norms] pre_gemma = <input_layernorm>`. |

### `[layer.dsv41_attn]`, `[layer.dsv41_moe]` (DeepSeek-V4.1, `recipes/deepseek_v41.toml`)

Name the checkpoint layout of the DeepSeek-V4.1 graph (`intarsia_core::dsv41`, contract in docs/design/dsv41-ops.md):
`prefix` (the attention / MoE tensors), `hc` (the hyper-connection mix weights of the sub-block), `norm` (its pre-norm)
and, on the attention, `engram` (the Engram projection on `engram_layer_ids`). The graph itself is code and reads
`config.json` directly; family `deepseek_v41` refuses to load for generation until the executing lanes land, and
`intarsia plan show --model <dir>` lists its op sequence from the safetensors headers alone.

### `[top]` (required)

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `embed` | string | required | Token embedding tensor. |
| `final_norm` | string | required | Final norm tensor. |
| `lm_head.tensor` | string | required | Output projection tensor. |
| `lm_head.tied_to` | string | none | Tensor to reuse when `lm_head.tensor` is absent from the checkpoint (or `tie_word_embeddings` is set). A missing head without this is a load error. |

### `[defaults]`

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kv_dtype` | string | `"bf16"` | KV cache dtype: `bf16`, `f16`, `f32` or `fp8_e4m3`. Override per run with `--kv-dtype`. Anything but `bf16` changes numerics ([tuning.md](tuning.md)). |
| `max_batch` | int | `1` | Most sequences a run may decode together. `--max-batch N` above it is refused; without the flag the value is clamped to what the engine implements (continuous batching is Metal only, up to 8). |
| `fp8_act` | string | `"static"` | FP8 checkpoints: `"static"` quantises activations with the checkpoint's `input_scale` (W8A8), `"none"` keeps them 16-bit (W8A16). No effect on other formats. See [quant-moe.md](quant-moe.md). Override with `--fp8-act`. |
| `w4a4_as_w4a16` | bool | `false` | A checkpoint that declares plain `NVFP4` (weights AND 4-bit activations, W4A4) is refused by the loader (`Gemma4` layers) and not covered by the recipe in `recipe new` / `onboard`, because the engine runs NVFP4 weight-only (W4A16): a deviation from the declared scheme and from vLLM. `true` accepts that knowingly (Gemma-4 NVFP4 does). |
| `mxfp4_act` | string | unset (what the checkpoint declares) | MXFP4 checkpoints: `"dynamic"` runs the W4A4 a Quark checkpoint declares (dynamic MXFP4 activations), `"none"` keeps activations 16-bit (W4A16), `"fp8"` quantises each token's activations to fp8 e4m3 (W4A8; HIP only, other backends refuse it at load with a message). Precedence: `--mxfp4-act`, then `[tuning.<backend>] mxfp4_act`, then this key, then the checkpoint's declaration. No effect on a checkpoint without MXFP4 projections. `recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml` sets `"none"` (the Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4: full MMLU n=1425 W4A16 0.822 vs W4A4 0.802, `docs/results/2026-10-27-act27-27b-w4a16-mmlu.md`; cost at tp2: prefill -30%, decode -13..-19%); `--mxfp4-act dynamic` runs the declared W4A4. The same file overrides it on HIP with `[tuning.hip] mxfp4_act = "fp8"`, so CUDA and Metal keep W4A16. |

### `[tuning]` and `[tuning.<backend>]`

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prefill_chunk` | int, at least 1 | `256` (code default) | Tokens per prefill forward pass, for every backend. Override with `--prefill-chunk`. |
| `[tuning.<backend>] prefill_chunk` | int, at least 1 | the base value | Same, for one backend: `cpu`, `cuda`, `hip` or `metal`. A backend without a table uses the base value. |
| `mtp_draft_vocab` | int, multiple of 8 | `0` (the full head) | Default of `--mtp-draft-vocab` for every backend: the MTP drafter's argmax runs over the first N `lm_head` rows. Output is unchanged (the verify pass keeps the full head); only acceptance moves. `0` or unset: the full head. Set only where measured. |
| `[tuning.<backend>] mtp_draft_vocab` | int, multiple of 8 | the base value | Same, for one backend. `recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml` (Qwen3.8-27B) sets `[tuning.hip] mtp_draft_vocab = 65536`; CUDA and Metal are unmeasured and keep the full head. |
| `[tuning.<backend>] mtp_default_tp_k` | int > 0 | unset (off) | With in-process tensor parallelism (`--tp N`, N > 1) on that backend, one sequence and no `--spec` given: run `--spec mtp --spec-k K` (a lone `--spec-k N` without `--spec` keeps this default with k = N; where no default applies it warns and speculation stays off). Needs `[mtp]` and a dense MTP head in the checkpoint (else plain decode with a note). `--spec off` or `INTARSIA_SPEC_DEFAULT=0` opts out; a configured prefix store (`--prefix-store`, `INTARSIA_PREFIX_STORE`) skips the default with one line (a drafting request bypasses the store). Per backend only (lane dfh, docs/results/2026-10-26-dfh-hip-dflash.md). |
| `[tuning.<backend>] mxfp4_act` | string | unset (the `[defaults]` value) | MXFP4 checkpoints: the activation mode on that backend when `--mxfp4-act` is not given (`"dynamic"`, `"none"` or `"fp8"`, as in `[defaults] mxfp4_act`). For a mode only some backends implement: `recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml` sets `"fp8"` under `[tuning.hip]` (W4A8: full MMLU n=1425 0.8204 vs W4A16 0.822; against W4A16 at tp2 prefill +48%, decode +11%; KL to the W4A16 golden 12x below W4A4's; `docs/results/2026-10-27-w4a8-hip-fp8-act.md`). A backend with no kernels for the mode refuses an explicit `--mxfp4-act fp8` at load. |
| `[tuning.<backend>] mtp_default_k` | int > 0 | unset (off) | With one rank (no `--tp`) on that backend, one sequence and no `--spec` given: run `--spec mtp --spec-k K` (a lone `--spec-k N` without `--spec` keeps this default with k = N). Needs `[mtp]` and the MTP head in the checkpoint (else plain decode with a note). `--spec off` or `INTARSIA_SPEC_DEFAULT=0` opts out; `--max-batch` above 1 keeps plain decode; a configured prefix store (`--prefix-store`, `INTARSIA_PREFIX_STORE`) skips the default with one line. Set for the Qwen3.6-35B on CUDA (`recipes/qwen3_5_moe.toml`, `mtp_default_k = 2`): decode 1.17-1.5x per category, prefill within 1 % of `--spec off` (lane mpf, docs/results/2026-10-27-mpf-macro-prefill-mtp.md), and for the Qwen3.8-27B on CUDA (`recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml` `[tuning.cuda]`, with `mtp_draft_vocab = 65536`): decode x1.70 at 1k, prefill unchanged (lane s27d, docs/results/2026-10-27-s27d-cuda-27b-decode.md). |
| `[tuning.<backend>] busy_chunk` | int >= 1 | unset (the loader's rule: the model's prefill chunk for the batched recurrent models, else 256) | Rows of a prefill chunk that runs beside decoding sequences under `serve --max-batch` > 1, on that backend; `--busy-chunk` wins, and the engine clamps it to the model chunk. `recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml` sets 256 on HIP next to `prefill_chunk = 2048`: a request alone prefills in 2048-row chunks, one arriving beside decoding streams in 256-row chunks, so their per-token stall stays at 135 ms (a 2048-row chunk stalls them 650 ms). |
| `[tuning.<backend>] tp_partial` | `"f32"` or `"bf16"` | unset (`f32`) | Tensor parallelism (`--tp N`, N > 1) on that backend: the dtype of the row-parallel partials (attention o, FFN down, GatedDeltaNet out) the all-reduce sums. `f32`: each rank keeps its partial in f32 and the sum is rounded to bf16 once, as one unsharded matmul would; `bf16`: each rank rounds its partial to bf16 and the all-reduce sums in place (half the bytes, two roundings per reduce). `INTARSIA_TP_PARTIAL=f32\|bf16` wins over the recipe. `recipes/qwen3_5_vl.toml` sets `"bf16"` under `[tuning.hip]` (Qwen3.8-27B at tp2 on the R9700s: prefill +17 % at 1k / 4k / 16k, MMLU n=1425 0.8218 against 0.8204, `docs/results/2026-10-27-tpb-hip-tp-partials.md`); every other backend and model keeps `f32`. Greedy ids differ from the f32 partials' ids. |
| `prefill_peel`, `[tuning.<backend>] prefill_peel` | int, 0..255 | `0` (off) | Prefill tail peel in rows: a forward pass longer than 256 rows whose length mod 256 is 1..=N runs those last rows as their own pass, as the default 256-row schedule cuts them, so a larger chunk gives the default chunk's bits where every kernel is row-invariant above N rows (`crates/intarsia-core/src/scheduler.rs` `peel_tail`). Same resolution as `prefill_chunk`; `INTARSIA_PREFILL_PEEL` overrides it. No builtin recipe sets it: for Qwen3.8-27B on HIP, `--prefill-chunk 4096` with `INTARSIA_PREFILL_PEEL=16` is bitwise chunk 256 and +35-43 % prefill, but under `serve --max-batch 16` it costs context and runs 4096-row busy chunks (docs/results/2026-10-25-mx-hip-27b-prefill.md section 4). |
| `prefill_peel_period`, `[tuning.<backend>] prefill_peel_period` | int, at least 1 | `256` | Period of the tail peel above: a pass longer than N rows whose length mod N is 1..=`prefill_peel` is cut (`peel_tail`); `prefill_peel` must be below it. Same resolution as `prefill_peel`; `INTARSIA_PREFILL_PEEL_PERIOD` overrides it. Set it to the busy chunk when the peel must cut only where that schedule ends a pass in a short tail: Qwen3.6-35B on Metal sets peel 8, period 2048 (docs/results/2026-11-04-m35-peel-period.md). `plan show` and the prefix-store key carry it only when it is not 256. |

Order of resolution: `--prefill-chunk`, then `[tuning.<backend>]`, then `[tuning]`, then 256; `plan show` prints which
one won. `--mtp-draft-vocab` resolves the same way (flag, `[tuning.<backend>]`, `[tuning]`, then the full head; the load log names the source). The chunk is a numerics knob, so commit a value only with the measurement behind it in a comment
([tuning.md](tuning.md)).

### `[config]` (rename `config.json` keys)

Every key is a string naming the `config.json` field to read (looked up in `text_config` first for multimodal
wrappers). Omit the table unless the family names a field differently from Hugging Face's usual.

| Key | Default |
|---|---|
| `hidden_size` | `"hidden_size"` |
| `num_layers` | `"num_hidden_layers"` |
| `num_heads` | `"num_attention_heads"` |
| `num_kv_heads` | `"num_key_value_heads"` |
| `head_dim` | `"head_dim"` (falls back to `hidden / heads` when the config has none) |
| `intermediate_size` | `"intermediate_size"` (with `block_auto_adjust_ff_dim = true`, LFM2, the dense FFN width is `int(2 * ff / 3)` times `block_ffn_dim_multiplier`, rounded up to `block_multiple_of`, as HF `Lfm2MLP` does) |
| `vocab_size` | `"vocab_size"` |
| `rms_eps` | `"rms_norm_eps"` |
| `rope_theta` | `"rope_theta"` |
| `tie_embeddings` | `"tie_word_embeddings"` |
| `max_positions` | `"max_position_embeddings"` |
| `layer_types` | `"layer_types"` (hybrid models) |
| `linear_k_heads`, `linear_v_heads` | `"linear_num_key_heads"`, `"linear_num_value_heads"` |
| `linear_k_head_dim`, `linear_v_head_dim` | `"linear_key_head_dim"`, `"linear_value_head_dim"` |
| `linear_conv_kernel` | `"linear_conv_kernel_dim"` |
| `short_conv_kernel` | `"conv_L_cache"` (LFM2's short conv; absent from the config = no such block) |

### `[accuracy]` (read only by `intarsia accuracy`; no effect on loading or serving)

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat_turns` | string | none | Turn format of the model's chat template (`"chatml"`): which rows of a chat prompt the model is asked to predict; the KL floor skips system and user turns. Fallback for a golden whose metadata names no known format. |

Thanks for reading that. I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed at work lately, there is too much on my plate and I keep procrastinating. Can you talk me through how you would approach this, and be honest and kind about it?

input:
I pasted a long document below, a bit of reading from earlier today.

code pass's 83 collectives; a prefill chunk stays on NCCL) straight over RDMA instead of NCCL: a stage kernel copies the partial into pinned host memory, a host proxy thread posts an RDMA write with immediate to the peer, a collect kernel waits for its flag and writes bf16(own + peer). Plain stream work, so it records into the CUDA graphs. Takes its devices and GID from `NCCL_IB_HCA` (two names under auto, one or two when required; no ports) and `NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX` (default 3); the queue pairs use NCCL's own link settings (timeout 20, 7 retries, about 34 s before a dead link errors). libibverbs is loaded with dlopen when the ring is opened, so the binary starts without it. The two ranks exchange their settings and every setup step on the control stream (unset or `auto` with `0` on the other rank = NCCL; `1` with `0` = error). A failed ring (a work completion error, a lost rank, the deadline below) makes the waiting kernels trap, the pass errors, and a tp-remote server marks itself failed (`/health` 503) and exits with code 87 while the worker leaves too, for a restart of both ranks. docs/results/2026-11-02-dsv41-rdma.md. | no (bitwise the NCCL pair: `a + b` commutes at world 2, one round to nearest even) |
| `INTARSIA_DSV41_RDMA_DEADLINE_S` | `crates/intarsia-backend-cuda/src/rdma.rs` | 180 (at least 1, at most 3600; anything else is the default) | Seconds a device wait of the RDMA ring (the collect kernel waiting for the peer's data, the stage kernel waiting for a free slot) may last before the kernel traps and the pass fails. Above the 34 s a dead link takes to report, below the 600 s the primary waits for a rank's answer; a rank that is paused for longer than this (stalled on disk, under memory pressure, SIGSTOP) fails the group. Short values are for tests. | n/a |
| `INTARSIA_DSV41_RDMA_FAULT` | `crates/intarsia-backend-cuda/src/rdma.rs` | unset | Test only (failure tests of the RDMA ring): `qp-err:N[:RAIL]` moves the queue pair of a rail (default 0) to the error state after this rank's N-th send, as after a fatal link error; `mute:N` keeps the rank alive but posts no send after its N-th (the peer's wait can end only by the device deadline); `ping` fails the setup's host ping; `nolib` pretends libibverbs is missing. Set on one rank to fault that rank. | n/a |
| `INTARSIA_BIND_RETRY_S` | `crates/intarsia-cli/src/cmd/serve.rs` | 120 | Seconds a supervised server keeps trying a port in use or an address not available, with the model loaded, before it exits 78 and the supervisor stops. Other bind errors, and a server without a supervisor, fail at once. | n/a |
| `INTARSIA_DSV41_FAILPATH_CHILD` | `crates/intarsia-models/src/dsv41_engine.rs` | unset | Test only. Set by `failpath_tests` of `dsv41_engine.rs` on the child process that runs rank 1 through `serve_group`, whose exit code is what the test checks. | no |
| `INTARSIA_DSV41_TEST_RANK0_FAIL_PASS` | `crates/intarsia-models/src/dsv41_engine.rs` | unset | Test only (`scripts/dsv41-tp2/failpaths-test.sh`): rank 0's forward pass after N more of them, counted after the warm-up, fails with `Error::Memory` once it was sent to the other rank, as a failed `cudaMalloc` would. The group must fail: HTTP 500, /health 503, both ranks exit 87. | no (the failing pass does not run; unset, nothing changes) |
| `INTARSIA_DSV41_SPEC_CHOOSE` | `crates/intarsia-models/src/dsv41_engine.rs:755` | on (`0` = fixed k) | DeepSeek-V4.1 speculative decoding: picks k per round from the confidence head (expected tokens per ms, up to `INTARSIA_DSV41_SPEC_K`, 0 allowed: the plain one-row pass). `INTARSIA_DSV41_SPEC_MIN_CONF` applies only with `0`. | no (with split-K verify passes a verify row is bitwise the decode row) |
| `INTARSIA_DSV41_SPEC_ROUND_MS` | `crates/intarsia-models/src/dsv41_engine.rs:809` | `31.1,36.5,41.2,46.0,50.8` | The ms table of `INTARSIA_DSV41_SPEC_CHOOSE`: a pass of 1, 2, .. rows, comma separated. Measured with `INTARSIA_DSV41_SPEC_TRACE=1` and `scripts/dsv41-tp2/roundcost.py`; before 2026-11-02 it was `31.3,38.1,42.9,47.8,52.7`. Retune when a pass gets faster (changing it alone moved nothing measurable: the same document). | no |
| `INTARSIA_DSV41_SPEC_DRAFT_MS` | `crates/intarsia-models/src/dsv41_engine.rs:814` | 5.5 (9.0 before the draft round moved onto the device) | The same rule's cost of a round outside its forward pass, ms (`roundcost.py`: the round's period minus its pass). | no |
| `INTARSIA_DSV41_SPEC_TRACE` | `crates/intarsia-models/src/dsv41_engine.rs:766` | unset (off) | DeepSeek-V4.1 speculative decoding: `1` prints one stderr line per round (drafts verified, their confidence logits, drafts accepted, the draft block's, the forward pass's and the round's ms), for working out offline what another k or floor would have done (`scripts/dsv41-tp2/specround.py`; the table costs: `scripts/dsv41-tp2/roundcost.py`). | no |
| `INTARSIA_DSV41_CAP` | `crates/intarsia-models/src/dsv41_engine.rs:13` | 32768 | DeepSeek-V4.1 token capacity of the (single) sequence: sizes the shared compressed-KV / index-key slots. Both TP ranks must agree (handshake). | no |
| `INTARSIA_DSV41_CHUNK` | `crates/intarsia-models/src/dsv41_engine.rs:13` | `--prefill-chunk`, else 2048 (default flipped from 512 on 2026-11-04, user decision) | DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill chunk (rows per pass). Both TP ranks must agree (handshake). 2048 is the chunk TensorFold serves and reads the routed experts once per 2048 rows instead of per 512 (the MoE launcher's prompt slice is 2048 rows, `kPromptRows`): a ~4.1K prompt prefills in 5.28 s instead of 6.75 s at 512, ~1K in 1.51 s instead of 1.76 s (docs/results/2026-11-02-dsv41-prefill.md); mean TTFT 24 % lower on 31K and 64K prompts (docs/results/2026-11-04-dsv41-chunk32k-quality-2.md). **Memory budget:** the workspace is sized at load for the chunk and is linear in it (rank 0: 0.304 GiB at 512, 0.577 at 1024, 1.136 at 2048, 4.41 at 8192; nearly independent of `INTARSIA_DSV41_CAP`: 0.300 at cap 8300, 0.302 at 33000), so 2048 costs 0.83 GiB more per rank, and with the CUDA context / NCCL rest 1.45 GiB less MemAvailable after warm-up (cap 66000: 9.86 GiB at 512, 8.41 at 2048). The state is 0.203 GiB per sequence at cap 66000 (0.104 at 33000), ~3 MiB per 1K tokens. I pasted a long document below, a bit of reading from earlier today.


```
intarsia accuracy ... --golden G --write-baseline golden/baselines/NAME.json   # record this run
intarsia accuracy ... --golden G --baseline golden/baselines/NAME.json         # no worse than that, plus margins
```

A baseline stores, per mode and per prompt: positions, top-1, mean KL, 21-way KL, top-5, tail masses, the mean
per-position |tail difference|, the largest single-position 21-way KL, greedy match; the identity of the golden (file
name, size, FNV-1a 64 of its bytes, prompt and position counts, its provenance metadata); the run configuration (model,
backend, device, KV dtype, activation dtype, fp8 mode, prefill chunk, decode positions, gate class); **the code that
produced it** (below); and how it was executed (command line, kernel disable list, resolved kernel per op). It is written
even when the absolute floor fails in that run (it then records `floor_pass: false`). The gate then requires, per mode,
with these default margins (flags in brackets):

| metric | allowed regression |
|---|---|
| top-1 | -0.3 pt (`--margin-top1`), but never less than one position (100/n pt: one flip must not fail a 160-position mode) |
| mean KL, 21-way KL | x1.15 (`--margin-kl`) and at least +1e-6 absolute (a baseline near zero is not brittle) |
| top-5 | -0.5 pt (`--margin-top5`), at least five overlap units (100/n pt) |
| `\|tail excess\|` (signed mean) | may grow by 0.002 (`--margin-tail`) over the baseline's |
| mean `\|tail difference\|` per position | may grow by 0.002 (`--margin-tail`): the signed mean lets positions that lose and gain tail mass cancel |
| largest single-position 21-way KL | x2.5 (`--margin-max-kl`), at least +1e-3 (a maximum is a noisy statistic) |
| **each prompt**: mean 21-way KL | x1.75 (`--margin-prompt-kl`), at least +1e-5; with `--noise-envelope` at least baseline + k x the prompt's measured noise |
| **each prompt**: top-1 | -1 pt, but at least one position; and each prompt's `\|tail difference\|` +0.002; same widening with an envelope |
| non-finite rows | none |

The per-prompt rows exist because the aggregate hides one prompt that got worse: with 10 prompts, one doubling its KL moves
the mean by about 10% and passes the x1.15 gate (unit test `one_prompt_doubling_fails_although_the_overall_mean_passes`).
The x2.5 / x1.75 factors are the smallest that let a legitimate bf16 reordering through on the one model that could be
measured here and still fail a 2x larger change; see "Choosing the self-golden budgets" for the data and its limits.
**On MoE and hybrid models these fixed per-prompt margins are inside the noise** (the 35B moves one prompt by KL 0.13-0.17
between two equally correct builds); the aggregate checks were kept hard by design, but the same experiment measured them inside the noise on `35b-long` too (docs/results/2026-10-13-phase1b.md 10.0). The per-prompt part is calibrated with a noise envelope
("Noise envelope" below). Without one the gate keeps the fixed margins and warns when `config.json` shows experts or
linear-attention layers.

It **refuses to compare** (before running anything) when the golden differs (hash, size, prompt or position count: a
regenerated golden needs a new baseline), when the KV dtype, backend, activation dtype, fp8 mode, prefill chunk, decode
positions or kernel disable list differ (`--allow-config-mismatch` downgrades the configuration part to a warning; the
golden must always match), and when the code stamp is not a legitimate "before" (next section). A different device name
is a warning only. The output keeps the verdicts apart: `floor verdict` (class thresholds) and `baseline verdict`, and
for the per-prompt part it prints every prompt and check with baseline value, this run, the limit and where the limit came
from (`fixed` or `envelope`), plus the envelope delta and the `k` that would have been needed. Verify a baseline in a
second process (the engine is deterministic run to run, so a run passes its own baseline with equal numbers; that needs
`--allow-same-code`). Baselines live in `golden/baselines/` (tracked, unlike the large `*.safetensors`).

### Noise envelope: per-prompt limits that follow the noise (`--write-noise-envelope`, `--noise-envelope`)

**Why.** The fixed per-prompt margins (KL x1.75, top-1 -1 pt or one position, `|tail diff|` +0.002) were set on a dense
model, where an equally correct build moves a prompt by almost nothing. On the MoE / hybrid 35B they sit inside the noise:
the same build with SIMT instead of flash attention, or with prefill chunk 256 instead of 1024, moves one prompt's 21-way
KL by 0.13-0.17 (`chat_reuse_4k`) and the others by 0.005-0.012, and the old build fails its own baseline gate when only
the attention kernel changes (docs/results/2026-10-13-phase1b.md, sections 8-10). A limit smaller than the spread of
correct builds measures that spread, not a defect. The 8B dense model is quiet (old vs new mean KL about 1e-10), so it
does not need this.

**Record it** (the same build as the baseline, a second time, with a declared equally correct perturbation):

```
intarsia accuracy ... --golden G --write-baseline B.json                                  # run 1, unperturbed
intarsia accuracy ... --golden G --noise-ref B.json --noise-perturb attn-simt --write-noise-envelope E.json
intarsia accuracy ... --golden G --noise-ref B.json --noise-perturb chunk=64  --write-noise-envelope E.json   # extends E.json
```

`--noise-perturb` is `chunk` (the baseline's prefill chunk / 4, at least 16), `chunk=N`, `attn-simt` (cuda / hip: sets
`INTARSIA_CUDA_DISABLE` / `INTARSIA_HIP_DISABLE` to the flash and split-KV attention kernels, the SIMT ones remain) or
`external:TEXT` (you set other flags or environment yourself, e.g. `INTARSIA_CPU_FAULT=matmul:4.7e-3` on the cpu backend,
and say what in TEXT). The run is refused unless it is the same golden, the same configuration except the declared
perturbation, the same build as the one that recorded `B.json` (code stamp equal), and it really changed something. For
each prompt and mode the envelope keeps both runs' numbers and the delta the per-prompt gate looks at: |top-1 difference|
in points, |mean 21-way KL difference|, |mean `|tail diff|` difference|; the largest single-position KL difference is
recorded and printed but no check uses it (there is no per-prompt max-KL check). A second perturbation into the same file
makes the per-prompt maximum count. The exit status of an envelope run does not depend on its own gates; it also prints
the perturbed run judged by the fixed margins, which is the quickest way to see that a margin is inside the noise.
A perturbation that does not reach a prompt (a prefill chunk change leaves every prompt shorter than the chunk
bit-identical) gives delta 0 for it: that is "not measured", not "quiet", and the writer and the gate both list those
prompts; the fixed margin applies to them.

**Use it**: `intarsia accuracy ... --golden G --baseline B.json --noise-envelope E.json [--envelope-k 2]`. The envelope is
refused unless it was measured against this golden, this baseline run configuration and the build that recorded `B.json`.
Per prompt and check:

```
limit = baseline value -/+ max(fixed margin, k x envelope delta of that prompt)        k = 2 by default
```

The verdict prints for every prompt and check the baseline value, this run, the limit, its source (`fixed`, or `envelope`
when k x delta was wider), the envelope delta, and the `k needed` for that check to pass, followed by the number of
failing prompts at k = 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10. **The aggregate (all-prompt) checks keep their fixed margins and stay hard**; the
envelope never touches them. Without `--noise-envelope` the per-prompt checks behave as before and the run warns when
`config.json` shows experts or linear-attention layers (a dense model gets no warning).

**Choosing k.** `k = 2` was fixed before the 35B re-evaluation; it says "a new build may move a prompt twice as far as
two correct builds of the old code moved it". It is the low end of what is defensible, and the numbers show where:

* The new build's difference to the baseline and the envelope's difference are two draws of the same noise (they share the
  baseline run), so even a correct build exceeds `k x delta` sometimes. Monte Carlo of one upper-limit check (normal noise;
  Laplace and t3 are slightly worse), fraction of correct builds that fail it, by number m of real perturbations in the
  envelope (the maximum is used):

  | m | k = 1 | k = 2 | k = 3 | k = 5 | k = 10 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 25 % | 13.6 % | 9.1 % | 5.5 % | 2.8 % |
  | 2 | 16.8 % | 5.5 % | 2.6 % | 1.0 % | 0.2 % |
  | 3 | 12.5 % | 2.7 % | 0.9 % | 0.2 % | 0 |
  | 4 | 10.0 % | 1.5 % | 0.4 % | 0.1 % | 0 |

  A gate has about 2 modes x 10 prompts x 3 checks, so with one or two perturbations k = 2 flags some prompt of a correct
  build most of the time.
* Measured on the Mac (Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B, cpu, `INTARSIA_CPU_FAULT=matmul:p` as the equally correct perturbation, p =
  4.7e-3 is the size of the old/new MoE kernel difference; 10 prompts x prefill and decode; the envelope's chunk 64
  perturbation moved nothing, 19 of 20 prompts bit-identical): correct builds of other p / other random draws failed
  1 prompt with m = 1 (1 of 1 trials) and with m = 2 (2 of 2: one prompt each in `code` + `chat_short`, `chat_system` + an
  aggregate max-KL); with m = 4 and m = 7 one of 4 trials failed (`chat_system`, a single position KL 0.15, an outlier no
  sample of the envelope had). Logs, envelopes and the driver scripts: `docs/results/2026-10-13-phase1b-acceptance/gate-calibration/mac/` (the scripts hard-code the scratch directory they ran in; the Monte Carlo is `scripts/mc.py`, run with `uv run --with numpy`).
* A bug is far outside: attention output x1.05 failed 7/6 aggregate checks and 10 of 10 prompts in both modes; x1.01 failed
  mean KL, tail-bucket KL and top-5 in prefill, mean KL in decode, and 3 + 1 prompts with the envelope (3 + 3 with fixed
  margins only: on this dense model the envelope removes none of them); `matmul:1.0` (every output one ulp off, 14x the
  rel_l2 of the envelope's perturbation) failed 9 + 7 prompts and the aggregates; x1.002 is not distinguishable from a
  correct build (the same prompt `code` that a correct build failed). 2x the envelope's rel_l2 (`matmul:2e-2`) failed one
  prompt per mode and the prefill aggregate top-1: the resolution of the gate is about a factor of 2 in rel_l2.

So: treat k = 2 as a pre-registered default, not as a calibrated false-positive rate. A prompt that fails with `k needed`
below about 3 is inside the spread of correct builds; one with `k needed` above 5 is not. For a hard per-prompt verdict
record at least 4 perturbations or raise `--envelope-k`; with one or two (all the 35B window could afford) read the
`k needed` column next to the verdict.

### Which code produced a baseline (provenance)

Review finding 1: the "before" baseline used to be recorded from the new tree with kernels switched off, and nothing
said which code made it. Switching off kernels cannot switch off the device-position rope / kv_append / attention
kernels, the split-KV grid or the loader changes, and a typo in `INTARSIA_CUDA_DISABLE` silently left the new kernel on.
Now:

* A build stamps itself. `INTARSIA_BUILD_STAMP` (the output of `scripts/tree-stamp.sh`: `head=<sha> code-tree=<hash>
  dirty=yes|no`, plus `overlay=<paths>`) is passed to `cargo build` and read with `option_env!`. The build boxes get the
  tree without `.git`, so the binary cannot ask git itself; `scripts/phase1b-acceptance.sh` computes the stamp on the Mac.
  A binary built without it is "unstamped" and its baselines and self-goldens are refused.
* A baseline and a self-golden store that stamp. The gate (`--pre-change SHA`, `--revlist FILE`) accepts a baseline only if
  its head is the declared pre-change commit or an ancestor of the code under test (`git rev-list HEAD` of that tree,
  written where the history is), the two code trees differ (a self-comparison proves nothing: `--allow-same-code` for
  reproducibility checks), and the baseline's tree is clean. The one allowed exception is the **harness overlay**: the
  pre-change engine has no baseline or self-golden support, so "before" is a build of the pre-change commit plus only the files
  in `HARNESS_OVERLAY_PATHS` (`accuracy.rs` and its three submodules, which read engine output and never change it). Its
  stamp says `dirty=yes overlay=...` and the gate accepts exactly that. The build under test must be clean (`--allow-dirty`
  for development).
* Kernel disable list: a baseline recorded with `INTARSIA_CUDA_DISABLE` / `INTARSIA_HIP_DISABLE` set is refused (it is not
  the pre-change code). The variables themselves now reject names that match no registered kernel when the device opens.
* Printed, never refused: `--no-graphs`, the resolved kernel per op, differences from the recorded run. If nothing differs
  the run says so ("a kernel or graph change cannot show up in this comparison").

### Same-weights regression gate: `--write-self-golden` / `--self-golden`

Review finding 2: against a vLLM reference with an fp8 KV cache the 35B baseline mean KL is about 6.5e-3, mostly the
reference's own noise, so "no worse than x1.15" allows about 1e-3 nats of real regression. When the weights are the
same the right reference is the previous build's own distribution:

```
# the pre-change build (4963b43 + harness overlay), once
intarsia accuracy --model M --backend cuda --golden G --write-baseline B.json --write-self-golden S.safetensors
# the new build
intarsia accuracy --model M --backend cuda --golden G --baseline B.json --pre-change 4963b43 --revlist revlist   # floor, baseline, per prompt
intarsia accuracy --model M --backend cuda --self-golden S.safetensors --pre-change 4963b43 --revlist revlist    # same weights
```

The dump keeps, for every prompt of G, the top-64 log-probs (full-vocabulary normalised, so the tail mass is known) of the
**prefill** path (every position) and of the **decode** path (the teacher-forced window, which is what graph replay and
the decode MoE kernel changed). It is a `intarsia-golden-topk-v1` file for the prefill rows (`--golden S` works), with
`dec_pos_i`, `dec_topk_ids_i`, `dec_topk_logprobs_i` for the decode rows and `self_golden=1`, the code stamp and the run
configuration in the metadata. Each path is compared with the same path of the old build, never prefill with decode, with
the same comparator as everything else (top-1, KL on the top-64 support, 21-way KL with the tail bucket). Budgets, all
flags, and the output line `SELF-STATS ...` the acceptance script reads:

| check | flag | default |
|---|---|---|
| mean 21-way KL(old \|\| new) | `--self-max-kl` | 1e-4 |
| largest single-position 21-way KL | `--self-max-pos-kl` | 5e-3 |
| top-1 flips, percent of positions (at least one position) | `--self-max-flip-pct` | 0.5 |
| mean per-position `\|tail difference\|` | `--self-max-tail` | 5e-4 |
| worst prompt's mean KL | `--self-prompt-factor` x `--self-max-kl` | 5 x |
